title: Modern Java, reflection, and modules — Module Quiz
description: Course assessment: Model API outcomes and inspect explicit application metadata.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: What does a sealed hierarchy make explicit?

options.text: A unique thread for each subtype

questions.prompt: Which annotation retention is needed for ordinary runtime reflection?
questions.explanation: Runtime retention preserves metadata for reflective inspection.

questions.prompt: Which JPMS directive permits reflective access to a package?

options.text: exports alone for all private access

questions.explanation: opens controls deep reflective access under module rules.

options.text: A custom runtime image from a module graph

questions.explanation: jlink assembles the required runtime modules.

questions.prompt: Does reflection remove compile-time safety concerns?

options.text: No, it often moves checks to runtime

questions.explanation: Lookup and invocation can fail at runtime.

questions.prompt: What happens to an exhaustive sealed-type switch when an uncovered permitted subtype is added and code is recompiled?

options.text: It must be updated or compilation fails

questions.explanation: Exhaustiveness checks expose the new alternative.
The sealed interface permits Success and Failure. The runtime value is a Success. The matching arm returns OK: saved. Null is outside this sample contract.
